key_insight: Raman and EXAFS reveal strong spin-lattice coupling in SrLaCoNbO6, with pronounced lattice anomalies well above the antiferromagnetic transition and signatures consistent with fluctuating Kitaev-like magnetic correlations.
engineering_relevance: The results highlight how local structural distortions and magnetoelastic effects can control functional behavior in correlated oxide materials, informing the design of spin-orbit-coupled quantum materials and devices.
method: Temperature-dependent Raman spectroscopy from high to low temperature
Co K-edge EXAFS to probe local bond distances and disorder
Analysis of phonon shifts, linewidths, Fano asymmetry, and low-energy continua
evidence_signal: The abstract reports anomalies near 60 K and 160–180 K in Raman and EXAFS observables, plus an excitation-energy-independent low-energy continuum supporting magnetic fluctuation effects.
watch_item: The authors note that purely structural contributions cannot be fully excluded, so the magnetic interpretation remains suggestive rather than definitive.
paper_title: Raman spectroscopic signature of Kitaev magnetism and complex spin-lattice coupling in S = 1/2 antiferromagnet SrLaCoNbO$_6$ double perovskite
